sections.name: Mushroom
sections.card:
Summary: An item that lets you roll two Dice Blocks instead of one and move the total of both. It costs 10 coins at an Item Shop and is Mario's favorite item.
Uses: Use it on your turn to roll two Dice Blocks and move the sum of the two numbers. Rolling the same number on both gives you 10 coins, and double 7s give you 20 coins.
Tips: At 10 coins it ties with the Skeleton Key as the cheapest item in the shop. You can carry only one item at a time, and with one in hand you cannot enter an Item Shop or start an Item Mini-Game, so use it before your next shop or Item Space.

sections.name: Golden Mushroom
sections.card:
Summary: An item that lets you roll three Dice Blocks and move the total of all three. It costs 20 coins at an Item Shop.
Uses: Use it to roll three Dice Blocks and move the sum of the three numbers. If all three show the same number you get 20 coins, and three 7s give you 50 coins.
Tips: From the middle of the game on, the shop's stock list for every placing includes it. On Bowser Land, walking past the Baby Bowser shop in a Bowser Suit makes him hand you one of four items for free: a Skeleton Key, Golden Mushroom, Boo Bell or Magic Lamp.

sections.name: Skeleton Key
sections.card:
Summary: An item that opens a locked gate on a board when you reach it, usually giving access to areas you could not otherwise reach. It costs 10 coins at an Item Shop and is Luigi's favorite item.
Uses: At a locked gate the key opens it, you are let through, and the gate locks again. Using one only opens the door, so you can spend it on a door without actually taking that path.
Tips: You cannot throw it away to make room for another item: it stays until you use it on a door, unless another player steals it. Item Shops sell it for 10 coins everywhere except Bowser Land, where Baby Bowser can force one on you for 12.

sections.name: Plunder Chest
sections.card:
Summary: An item that steals an item from an opponent. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Peach's favorite item.
Uses: Using it steals an item from an opponent picked at random out of all the opponents who are holding one; you cannot choose whom to rob. You can use the stolen item at once, unless it is a Bowser Bomb, or keep it for a later turn.
Tips: In the Item Shop it shows up for the player in second place in the middle of the game and for the player in first place in the last five turns.

sections.name: Dueling Glove
sections.card:
Summary: An item that lets you pick an opponent to duel in a Duel Mini-Game for coins. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Wario's favorite item.
Uses: Using it summons a Goomba, then you choose the opponent to duel and how many coins to wager. The most you can wager is the coin count of whichever of the two players has fewer coins before the duel.
Tips: The wager is always coins. In the Item Shop it appears in the middle of the game for third and fourth place and in the last five turns for first and second place.

sections.name: Warp Block
sections.card:
Summary: An item that swaps your place on the board with a random opponent. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Yoshi's favorite item.
Uses: A Warp Block appears above you when you use it, and hitting it warps you and swaps positions with a randomly chosen opponent. You can still roll the regular Dice Block on the same turn.
Tips: You can also win one from an Item Mini-Game. In the Item Shop it only shows up in the last five turns, for the players in second, third and fourth place, and on Bowser Land the forced sale costs 17 coins.

sections.name: Magic Lamp
sections.card:
Summary: An item that takes you straight to the Star Space. At 30 coins it is the most expensive item in the Item Shop.
Uses: Using it summons the Mushroom Genie, who gives you a ride to the Star Space, where you are asked whether you want to trade 20 coins for a Star.
Tips: You still pay 20 coins for the Star when you arrive, on top of the 30 it costs to buy. The shop offers it only in the last five turns, to third and fourth place. When Bowser's Multiplying Toads puts two Toads on the board, a Magic Lamp always takes you to the real one.

sections.name: Boo Bell
sections.card:
Summary: A rare item that calls a Boo to steal coins or a Star from an opponent. Neither kind of Item Shop sells it; you win it in an Item Mini-Game.
Uses: Using it summons a Boo, who asks whom to steal from. Stealing coins costs you five coins and stealing a Star costs 50 coins, and the Boo can take at most 30 coins or one Star.
Tips: If a Boo is stealing coins from you, press the A button quickly to fight it off. Baby Bowser's shop on Bowser Land can also give you a Boo Bell for free, as one of four possible gifts, if you pass it in a Bowser Suit.

sections.name: Bowser Suit
sections.card:
Summary: A rare item that disguises you as Bowser and lets you steal 20 coins from any opponent you pass. You usually win it in an Item Mini-Game.
Uses: When used you put on a full-body suit in the likeness of Bowser's body, and you steal 20 coins from any opponent you pass.
Tips: Wearing it changes how Baby Bowsers deal with you: the one on the board always gives you coins when you pass, and on Bowser Land you can change the parade's route for free unless it is the last move, collect 20 coins at the Bowser Bank and get a free item from the forced shop. The regular Item Shops do not sell the suit, but Baby Bowser's shop on Bowser Land can force one on you for 12 coins.

sections.name: Bowser Bomb
sections.card:
Summary: A rare item that is not yours to aim: if you get one, Bowser uses it at the end of the current turn, and anyone he passes loses all their coins. It is Donkey Kong's favorite item.
Uses: At the end of the turn Baby Bowser turns into Bowser, rolls three Dice Blocks and moves around the board that many spaces, taking all the coins from every player he passes.
Tips: Besides Item Mini-Games, the only way to get one is Baby Bowser's forced sale on Bowser Land, at 12 coins. If you steal one with a Plunder Chest you cannot use it right away. If it goes off while Bowser's Multiplying Toads has put two Toads on the board, it shows which Toad is the false one.
